Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Peak Brands Inc. Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. If you're using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Peak Brands Inc.'s Q3 results. With me on the call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and other members of our leadership team, including Lisa Patel, our Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. Peak Brands delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover four key aspects:
1. Gross margin percentage.
2. Competitive activity and response.
3. Geographic performance: developed versus emerging markets.
4. Promotional strategy and effectiveness.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Mike Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $2.85 billion, representing a 4.2% organic increase compared to the prior year. Gross margin was 48.2%, driven by targeted pricing and mix actions, productivity savings, input cost favorabilities, partially offset by foreign exchange headwinds. Operating income was $420 million. Diluted earnings per share were $1.25. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Let me unpack our gross margin performance in more detail. This quarter, gross margin came in at 48.2%, up a robust 210 basis points year-over-year and 120 basis points sequentially from Q2. This marks our strongest quarterly gross margin expansion in the past five years, excluding pandemic anomaly quarters, and puts us on track for our full-year target of 47.5% to 48.5%. For context, this compares favorably to peers like Mondelez, which reported around 46% in their last quarter amid similar cocoa headwinds, and even outperforms Procter & Gamble's beauty and fabric care segments at roughly 49% on a blended basis.

Starting with the headline math, revenue grew 4.2% organically to $2.85 billion, driven by a 5.1% price/mix tailwind partially offset by a modest 0.9% volume headwind as consumers traded down in certain value channels. Cost of goods sold came in at $1.48 billion, or 51.8% of sales—down from 53.9% a year ago. This delivered gross profit of $1.37 billion, up 12% year-over-year.

The 210 basis points expansion stemmed from four key drivers. First, pricing and mix actions contributed +310 basis points. We executed targeted pricing across 85% of our portfolio, averaging 6.2% globally, with standout increases in North America snacks at +8.1% and APAC beverages at +7.4%. This reflects our strong brand equity in icons like Peak Crunch bars—our direct competitor to Hershey's—where elasticities remained favorable at -1.2 despite inflation fatigue. Mix was a tailwind as premium segments grew double-digits: high-margin organic and plant-based SKUs now represent 28% of sales, up from 22% last year, shifting us away from low-margin private-label fillers.

Second, productivity and supply chain savings added +180 basis points. Our Peak Efficiency 2.0 program delivered $62 million in quarter-over-quarter savings, exceeding our $200 million annual run-rate goal by Q1. This includes AI-driven demand forecasting via partnerships with Palantir, which cut inventory obsolescence by 18% in our salty snacks plants, and robotic process automation in packaging lines across our Ohio and Mexico facilities, yielding 12% labor efficiency gains. We're also advancing sustainable sourcing: palm oil contracts locked at pre-Ukraine levels through RSPO-certified suppliers, saving $15 million versus spot pricing.

Third, input cost favorabilities netted +50 basis points. Raw material deflation in dairy (-3%) and corn (-5%) more than offset cocoa inflation (+22%, impacting our chocolate-coated nuts by $28 million). Overall input costs rose just 1.8%, versus the 4.5% CPI inflation rate for CPG commodities tracked by Bloomberg. Ocean freight normalized post-Red Sea disruptions, down 15% sequentially, though air freight for perishables in APAC remained elevated.

Fourth, foreign exchange and other factors created a -330 basis points headwind. Unfavorable FX, particularly the weakening Argentine peso and Turkish lira, shaved 220 basis points, as 22% of COGS is sourced internationally. We also absorbed one-time inventory write-downs of $12 million from phasing out low-margin legacy SKUs in household cleaners, part of our portfolio optimization echoing Unilever's divestitures.

Regionally, trends are positive across the board. North America, 55% of sales, hit 51.4% gross margin, up 280 basis points year-over-year, powered by pricing discipline in clubs and e-comm—Amazon velocity up 15%—and manufacturing leverage from our new Texas mega-plant, which boosted throughput by 25%. EMEA, 25% of sales, was at 45.8%, flat year-over-year amid energy surcharges and wheat volatility from Black Sea tensions, but with sequential gains from localized sourcing in Poland. APAC/LatAm, 20% of sales, reached 44.2%, up 150 basis points, with Brazil beverages benefiting from sugar deflation and China personal care from premiumization in platforms like Tmall.

This isn't a one-off—gross margins have expanded 450 basis points cumulatively over the past 18 months, reversing 2022 compression from post-COVID supply shocks when cocoa hit $4,000 per ton and polypropylene packaging surged 40%. We're embedding resilience through a zero-based budgeting refresh targeting 3-4% structural savings on variable costs like flexo-print packaging optimization; a premiumization ladder accelerating shifts to super-premium tiers—like Peak Glow skincare rivaling Dove's serums—aiming for 52%+ margins by 2026; and sustainability-linked incentives tying 10% of supplier volume to carbon reduction KPIs, projecting $100 million in savings by FY25 as Scope 3 emissions drop 20%.

Looking ahead, we see tailwinds from pricing normalization at +2-3% into Q4, productivity ramping to $75 million quarterly, and input stabilization as cocoa harvests recover per ICCO forecasts. Risks include geopolitical freight and potential El Niño impacts on coffee and palm, but our hedging covers 70% of 2024 exposure. We expect Q4 gross margin at 48.5-49.0%, positioning FY24 as a pivotal year in our margin re-rating story.

Now, shifting to competitive dynamics shaping our Q3 performance across key CPG categories—personal care, household essentials, and packaged foods—and our proactive responses. The CPG landscape remains fiercely contested, with inflation headwinds, shifting consumer behaviors toward value-seeking and premiumization, and intensifying pressure from branded peers and private labels. Latest NielsenIQ Total US scan data through Q3 shows industry-wide promotional intensity rose to 28% of ACV—up 3 percentage points year-over-year—driven by aggressive shelf price rollbacks and everyday low pricing strategies from players like Procter & Gamble and Unilever.

In personal care, competitive activity was particularly acute, with Colgate-Palmolive ramping up trade spend by an estimated 18% year-over-year to defend share in oral care, launching their Total Plaque Pro line at 10-15% below category average pricing to counter our premium positioning. Reckitt Benckiser accelerated innovation, rolling out a bio-based disinfectant wipe under Lysol that's gained 2.1 share points in multi-outlet distribution per IRI data, capitalizing on post-pandemic hygiene tailwinds. This pressured our margins in North America, where we saw a temporary 0.8-point market share dip to 22.4% in Q3.

Our response was multifaceted and data-driven. We used precision-targeted shopper marketing via our AI-powered dynamic pricing engine, optimizing in-store promotions to lift velocity by 12% on our flagship PureGlow Toothpaste line. We accelerated our Clean Label Renew initiative, reformulating three SKUs with 95% naturally derived ingredients—meeting Euromonitor's projected 15% CAGR in clean beauty through 2027—and secured 1,500 additional shelf facings in Walmart and Kroger, driving a 1.4-point share recovery to 23.8% by quarter-end. Trade spend efficiency improved to 14.2% of revenue, versus peers' 16-18%, thanks to our zero-based budgeting model.

In household essentials, Unilever's Persil brand executed a bold 20% temporary price promotion wave across EMEA, capturing 3.2 share points from incumbents amid softening volumes—EU household penetration for detergents fell 4% year-over-year per Kantar Worldpanel. Private labels, now at 28% category share in Western Europe (up from 24% in 2022), compounded this via Aldi/Lidl's ultra-low-cost pods. APAC saw similar intensity, with P&G's Ariel gaining 1.5 points in China through Douyin e-commerce bundling.

We responded with innovation-led differentiation. In North America, our EcoShield Pods launch—featuring 30% less water usage and Ocean Plastic packaging—achieved 85% distribution in 4 weeks, adding 450 basis points to household ACV and lifting category share to 19.6% (up 90 basis points year-over-year). In EMEA, we partnered with Carrefour for exclusive Sustainability Aisle placements, countering private labels with a 25% premium price architecture that resonated with 35% of value-conscious green shoppers, per our proprietary NPS tracking. In APAC, we deployed machine learning algorithms for hyper-localized pricing on Tmall, reducing stock-outs by 22% and growing e-com sales 35% year-over-year to $45 million.

Packaged foods faced volume wars, with Mondelez's Oreo and Cadbury executing 22% higher media GRPs to promote Share the Joy campaigns, stealing 1.1 share points in salty snacks amid a 2% category contraction. PepsiCo's zero-sugar Frito-Lay variants pressured our portfolio, especially in LatAm where inflation hit 50%+ in Argentina/Brazil. Overall, CPG snack promo depth averaged 22% off RRPs, per Circana data.

Our playbook emphasized portfolio optimization and DTC acceleration. We pruned underperforming SKUs (5% of portfolio) to fund a 15% uplift in A&P behind core brands like CrunchMax Bars, launching three ready-to-drink protein extensions that gained 2.3 share points in health-focused channels. In North America, we recaptured 1.2 points via Sam's Club velocity drivers, hitting 25.3 turns per store. LatAm response included localized Precio Justo hedging against FX volatility, stabilizing margins at 28% while growing volumes 8% through Mercado Libre integrations. Forward GRP allocation shifts 10% more to digital, targeting Gen Z via TikTok Shop for 20% cheaper customer acquisition cost than linear TV.

Across regions, we're seeing a bifurcation: value tiers growing 7% in volume driven by private labels and discounters like Dollar General, while premiums expand 12% in value via health/wellness claims—our sweet spot. We've insulated against this through $250 million in FY24 supply chain resilience investments, including nearshoring 30% of NA production to Mexico, cutting lead times 25%. Competitively, we're monitoring M&A ripples from Mars' Kellanova bid, positioning us for bolt-on deals in functional nutrition.

In summary, while competitive spend rose industry-wide, our share held flat at 14.2% globally per Nielsen, with organic growth of 4.1% outpacing category +1.8%. We're confident in our Win with Innovation and Execution framework—projecting 50 basis points share gain in Q4 through holiday velocity programs and sustained DTC ramp to 15% of sales.

Next, let's dive into our geographic performance, focusing on the divergence between developed and emerging markets—a cornerstone of our growth strategy in CPG, where we navigate mature, value-conscious dynamics in developed regions and high-volume, aspirational expansion in emerging ones.

In Q3, total net revenues reached $2.85 billion, up 5% as reported and 4.2% organically, excluding FX and M&A. Developed markets—62% of our portfolio, including North America, Western Europe, Japan, and Australia—delivered organic growth of 3.2%, driven by favorable price/mix of +4.1%, offset by a modest volume decline of -0.9%. This reflects the resilient but challenged consumer environment, similar to post-inflation stabilization at peers like Procter & Gamble and Unilever.

Emerging markets, 38% of revenues—from Latin America, Greater China, India, Southeast Asia, and Africa—posted robust organic growth of 12.8%, with volume up +7.6% and price/mix +5.2%. This underscores structural tailwinds of urbanization, rising middle-class incomes, and e-commerce penetration, fueling category expansion in snacks, beverages, and personal care.

In developed markets, North America—our largest at 35% of group sales—grew organically by 4.1%. Power Brands like Peak Crunch snacks and PureGlow skincare saw household penetration gains of +1.2 points per Nielsen data, thanks to targeted in-store executions and a 22% surge in e-commerce sales via Amazon and our D2C site. Price/mix was strong at +5.3%, reflecting premium shelf-space resets amid inflation—like our relaunch of Peak Zero Sugar beverages, capturing +180 basis points of ACV share in energy drinks.

Western Europe, 18% of sales, was softer at +1.8% organic, pressured by volume softness in mass-market laundry and household care, down -2.1% as consumers traded to private labels amid high energy costs. Premium beauty—led by LuxeClean haircare with 98% biobased ingredients—grew +9%, aligning with Euromonitor's 6% category growth in sustainable personal care. Japan and Australia added +2.5% combined, bolstered by aging demographics in nutritionals.

Key initiatives include our $250 million investment in AI-driven demand sensing across 15,000 SKUs in North America and Europe, improving forecast accuracy by 15%, reducing inventory obsolescence by 8%, and enabling just-in-time efficiencies—critical as we lap 2023 cocoa and palm oil spikes hitting Hershey and Mondelēz.

In emerging markets, Latin America surged +15.2% organically, led by Brazil and Mexico. Brazil's FizzUp carbonated drinks achieved double-digit volume growth of +11%, gaining +250 basis points market share per Kantar Worldpanel, via affordable multipacks and localized flavors like guava-mango for the informal trade channel dominating 60% of volume. Mexico saw personal care up +18% with AguaFresca body wash, riding rising female workforce participation.

Asia-Pacific ex-China delivered +14.5%, with India at +22% organic—volume +13%—fueled by rural penetration via Project Shakti micro-entrepreneur program, expanding Sambhar Spice snacks into 5,000 new villages, boosting distribution 12% and +300 basis points IRI share in savory snacks. Southeast Asia grew +12%, despite some Indonesia FX volatility. Greater China was +6.2% organic, volumes flat post-zero-COVID, but e-commerce on Tmall and JD.com jumped 28%, gaining traction in mid-tier cities with value packs of Peak Noodles for the 400 million-strong middle class.

Across emerging, $400 million capex in localized production—like new aseptic plants in India and Vietnam—de-risked supply chains, cutting lead times 25% and supporting 10%+ volume goals.

This bifurcation validates our bi-coastal portfolio: harvesting cash in developed markets—where EBIT margins expanded +110 basis points to 22.3% on pricing and zero-based budgeting—to fuel emerging investments, contributing 65% of group organic growth despite 38% of sales. Risks include currency headwinds shaving 2% off emerging growth and U.S. consumer sentiment dipping to 98.7 per Conference Board. Opportunities lie in sustainability—like 30% recycled packaging by 2025—to meet EU regs and appeal to Gen Z in India.

Forward, developed markets mid-single digits organically in FY24, emerging high-teens, driving group 8-10%. Our $1.2 billion Latin American hygiene acquisition positions +15% compounded growth there through 2027.

Finally, on our promotional strategy and effectiveness—a critical lever amid inflation, shifting shoppers, and competition from private labels and e-commerce like Amazon and Walmart+.

In Q3, total A&P spend was $405 million, up 8% year-over-year, or 14.2% of net sales. Trade promotions were 62% or $250 million; consumer promotions including digital coupons and loyalty rebates 25% at $100 million; media the balance. This reflects our ROI-disciplined model, prioritizing right-sized promotions over volume discounting.

We leaned into trade promotion optimization via our TPM 2.0 platform with AI forecasting from NielsenIQ and Circana, modeling depth, frequency, and timing at SKU-store level. For fabric care—like Tide performance—we reduced baseline trade spend 12% year-over-year while lifting distribution ACV 15% to 92% nationally in North America. ROI hit 3.2x, up from 2.7x, as incremental net merch volume return on TPM dollars. Clustering around high-velocity events like back-to-school avoided promotion cannibalization and forward-buying erosion.

For consumer-facing, our Everyday Rewards loyalty program integrated with Kroger and Target Circle drove 22% of Q3 volume. Targeted digital rebates via Ibotta and Fetch Rewards achieved 28% redemption—double Kantar's 14% industry average. For beverages like Gatorade, geo-fenced push notifications during heatwaves generated 19% sales lift in SMSA markets, boosting household penetration 4 points to 68%. ROI was 4.1x, with 65% redemptions converting to repeats within 30 days.

By geography: North America (52% of spend) was trade-heavy with Walmart/Costco; Price Lock on essentials mirrored P&G, with BOGO yielding 11% share gain in laundry vs. Unilever's Persil, though elasticities softened to -2.8. Europe (28%) pivoted to health bundles amid HFSS regs, seeing 14% volume growth in UK/Germany at 2.9x ROI, with ECR shrinkage collaborations cutting out-of-stocks 22%. Emerging (20%, +18% YoY spend) scaled via Carrefour Brazil and Reliance India; sachet-to-pouch on personal care drove 25% penetration lift in Southeast Asia at 3.5x ROI despite FX.

Industry promo ROI rebounded to 2.8x per Circana; we're ahead with +12 point net promoter lift vs. peers' +7, via ML models predicting 85% lift variance. Challenges: private labels +300 bps share forced pruning 15% SKUs, reallocating $50 million to cores. E-com promos contributed 9% volume, AOV +17% from bundling.

For Q4, 5-7% A&P increase skewed digital (35%), experiential like Taste the Future sampling, targeting 3.5x ROI and 200 bps category outperformance amid 2-3% slowdown.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your consumer spending habits?

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, John. Inflation continues to pressure consumer wallets, leading to some trade-down in value channels as we noted with the 0.9% volume headwind. However, our strong brand equity and premium mix shift—now 28% of sales—have kept elasticities favorable at -1.2, allowing us to pass through 6.2% pricing globally without significant share loss. In developed markets, we're seeing stability via e-comm growth, while emerging volumes remain robust at +7.6%. We're monitoring sentiment closely but confident our innovation pipeline cushions any further slowdown.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Johnson with JPMorgan.

Emily Johnson:
Regarding your new product EcoShield Pods, what are the projections for its market impact?

Lisa Patel:
Thanks, Emily. EcoShield Pods have been a standout, achieving 85% distribution in just four weeks and adding 450 basis points to household ACV in North America. We're projecting 2-3 share points gain in laundry by year-end, with $150 million in incremental sales for FY24, driven by sustainability appeal—30% less water and Ocean Plastic packaging resonating with green shoppers. EMEA rollout starts Q4 via Carrefour exclusives, targeting 15% category penetration by mid-2025. Early NPS is +45, well above benchmarks.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley.

David Lee:
Can you provide more details on the promotional spending for the quarter?

Mike Chen:
Sure, David. As I detailed earlier, A&P was $405 million or 14.2% of sales, up 8% year-over-year, with trade at 62%. Our TPM 2.0 AI platform delivered 3.2x ROI by optimizing cuts and timing, avoiding cannibalization—up from 2.7x last year. Consumer promos like Everyday Rewards hit 4.1x ROI with 28% redemptions. Regionally, emerging markets saw highest growth at 18% YoY spend. Q4 embeds 5-7% increase, focused digital for 3.5x blended ROI.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your questions and participation in today's call. We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Peak Brands Inc. Q3 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
